reuse.why: Extends the existing getScheduledAmount with an op parameter, reuses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance and mirrors getRangedAmountWorstCase with getApproxAmountWorstCase; forecast now calls the shared helper instead of its own dispatch.

duplication.why: No logic is copied, but schedule-template.ts keeps its own isbetween/isapprox/else op dispatch that duplicates what getScheduledAmount now decides.

placement.why: The approximate worst case lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the ranged worst case.

scope.why: Only the amount helper, its planning/posting callers and tests are touched.

maintainability.why: The op parameter is optional, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and the client balance still call getScheduledAmount without it, so previews ignore the new rule; stale 'rounded midpoint' comments in schedules/app.ts remain.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts dispatches on op itself to getRangedAmountWorstCase/getApproxAmountWorstCase instead of calling getScheduledAmount(value, false, op)

one_place.where: rule defined in shared/schedules.ts getApproxAmountWorstCase/getScheduledAmount(op), but computeSchedulePreviewTransactions (shared/schedules.ts) and desktop-client Balance.tsx do not pass op, and schedule-template.ts keeps its own op dispatch
